title: Cabinet approves Upgradation of the Muzaffarpur-Sitamarhi-Sonbarsa Section of NH-22 to 4-Lane Standard in Bihar on Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) at total Capital Cost of Rs.3590.73 crore
body_text:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved the Upgradation of the Muzaffarpur-Sitamarhi-Sonbarsa Section of NH-22 to four-Lane Standard in Bihar. The project will be developed on Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) at a total capital cost of Rs.3590.73 crore with a total length of 82.578 km.
The proposed project holds significant strategic and economic relevance due to its integration with Bihar’s expanding National Highway network. It acts as a key feeder corridor connecting the India–Nepal border at Sonbarsa with economic centers like Muzaffarpur at NH-27 (East–West Corridor). The project will significantly reduce congestion in densely populated areas of Muzaffarpur, Muksudpur, Runni Saidpur, Thumma, Dumra, Bhutahi, and Sonbarsa.
The project is expected to enable faster and safer movement of passengers and freight, improve travel efficiency and strengthen regional connectivity. It has been designed for a speed of 100 kmph with an average speed of 80 kmph, having no at-grade median openings, ensuring fast and safe travel.
Planned in accordance with the principles of the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, the project will enhance multimodal integration by improving connectivity to key economic, social and logistics nodes, including industrial areas and major railway stations. Improved connectivity will facilitate efficient movement of goods and agricultural supply chains, support regional economic growth, and provide better access to important cultural and religious destinations such as the Buddhist Circuit and historic Janaki Punaura Dham Temple, Sitamarhi.
The Muzaffarpur–Sitamarhi–Sonbarsa stretch of NH-22 holds significant strategic and economic relevance, ensuring seamless linkage to the national freight grid. It is in synergy with existing corridors such as NH-31 and NH-122 enhances connectivity to industrial zones like Barauni and riverine logistics hubs along the Ganga It also enhances cross-border passenger and cargo movement via the nearby Land Port at Bhithamore.
In addition, the project has provision for seven Major Bridges (including a 340m long major bridge over the perennial Bagmati River), three Railway Over Bridges (ROBs), and two Flyovers (1170m & 270m) to maintain cross movement of the traffic and ensure safe, high-speed travel.
The project will increase average travel speeds, reduce travel time, and improve overall road safety, fuel efficiency, and vehicle operating costs, thereby enhancing regional mobility and socio-economic development.
The project provides seamless connectivity to key economic, social, and logistics nodes across Bihar. Additionally, the upgraded corridor will enhance connectivity to five PM Gati-Shakti Economic Nodes (four Industrial Estates and one Mega Food park), four Social Nodes (Baba Garibnath Temple, Mata Janki Temple, Punaura Dham, Muzaffarpur & Sitamarhi aspirational Districts), and two Logistic Nodes (Muzaffarpur & Sitamarhi Railway Stations), thereby facilitating faster movement of goods and passengers across the region.

enrichment.summary: The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved upgrading the 82.578 km Muzaffarpur-Sitamarhi-Sonbarsa section of NH-22 in Bihar to four-lane standard, to be built under the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) at a capital cost of Rs.3590.73 crore. The corridor connects the India-Nepal border at Sonbarsa to Muzaffarpur on NH-27 (East-West Corridor), and includes seven major bridges, three railway over-bridges, and two flyovers. It is planned under the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan to improve multimodal connectivity to industrial, social, and logistics nodes.
enrichment.context: Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) is a public-private partnership model for highway construction where the government contributes 40% of project cost during construction and the remaining 60% is paid to the developer as annuity over the concession period, sharing risk between government and private players. It has become the dominant model for National Highway Authority of India (NHAI) projects after the decline of the pure BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer) toll model, addressing financing and risk-sharing concerns of private developers. This project is also framed under the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (launched 2021), which aims to integrate infrastructure planning across ministries by mapping economic, social, and logistics nodes for multimodal connectivity, reducing logistics costs, and avoiding fragmented, delayed project execution. Cross-border connectivity via Sonbarsa (adjoining Nepal) also has strategic significance given India's efforts to strengthen trade and connectivity links with Nepal. Such highway approvals are routine CCEA business but occasionally test aspirants on HAM mechanics, PM GatiShakti nodes, and highway network nomenclature (NH numbering, East-West Corridor).

prelims_questions.question: The 'Hybrid Annuity Mode' (HAM), often referred to in the context of national highway construction in India, involves:
options: Full cost of the project being borne by the private developer with recovery through tolls
Government paying 100% of the project cost upfront to the developer
Government contributing a portion of the project cost during construction, with the remainder paid as annuity over time
The project being fully funded through external commercial borrowings only
prelims_questions.explanation: Under HAM, the government typically contributes about 40% of the project cost during construction, while the remaining 60% is paid to the developer as annuity over the concession period, combining features of EPC and BOT models.

prelims_questions.question: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan primarily aims to:
options: Provide direct cash transfers to farmers for irrigation infrastructure
Integrate infrastructure planning across ministries for multimodal connectivity
Replace all toll-based highway projects with free highways
Finance only urban metro rail projects
prelims_questions.explanation: PM GatiShakti is a National Master Plan launched to ensure integrated planning and coordinated implementation of infrastructure connectivity projects across various economic and social nodes, improving multimodal connectivity and reducing logistics costs.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the Hybrid Annuity Mode (HAM) in India's national highway development compared to earlier BOT and EPC models. What challenges remain in its implementation?
Examine how the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan seeks to transform infrastructure planning in India, with reference to multimodal connectivity and regional economic development.
